posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
> **dave battin:** it really sucked that Dinesh removed all his posts, but on the other hand it was his option to do so, just as providing other voluntary profile information is any member’s option

I have to sharply disagree with that one, Dave. When Dinesh removed his posts, he severely damaged the forum, because his participation was so substantial, and so many people joined in the discussions with him. The contributions made by the other forum members were thus obviated to some extent in those threads, because the readers could no longer follow them.

I would in no way compare Dinesh's action to someone who does not have a filled-out profile, such as myself. This is simply a privacy measure, at least in my case. If someone wants to send me a private message, that's fine, and we can go from there.

As for the skypecasts, I wish you the best of success. It seems like it can be an excellent learning experience, because the best way to learn things quickly is by verbal communication, everything else being equal. No waiting around for answers.

On the other hand, the downside is that you have to suffer through all the "noise" that is not helpful. This takes considerable time, too. That's why I would like to make a suggestion: personally I would like to see more focused skype groups, and the person responsible for the skypecast should have a real interest in the area of focus. That way, the person responsible won't be wasting his time, and won't get discouraged. What do you think?

In my case, the area of interest would be "practical" DCG. Holography encompasses way, way too much to have a generalized skypecast, in my opinion. I don't want to sit through a physics lecture when I don't want to, when I could more easily pick up a book.

posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md:
Holography skypecasts were started as a means to help fellow holographers advance…thereby bringing the science of holography to a higher significance. In only four months, we have moved from just having group discussions to making them downloadable as podcasts for anyone to hear. As with most other things, the internet has brought holography information to the masses. Now we can pass information real time ... no longer does that frustrated student need to spend failed hours in the dark, or spend hours scouring libraries for outdated reference articles that may or may not have the answer to their exact challenge. The ability to help the budding and advanced holographer is immediate. That is where holography skypecast should go, and with this new technology moving as fast as it is, my nearly 50 year-old brain is having some difficulty keeping ahead of it all.

To maintain the integrity of the skypecast’s intent, the skypecast should remain on a stand alone site. Because the holography form inspired the idea for live holography discussions, I think it’s important to keep the forum link and use it as a reference for archived material. It might also serve as a permanent site for archived skypecasts.

This new stand alone site will be a donation run site with its sole purpose to conduct live skypecasts and maintain archived skypecasts/podcasts. Incorporateing a current event calendar and a weekly question board to store questions submitted during the week preceding the live skypecast would be a good idea.

Rotating hosts could be introduced every few months or whatever…this host can talk about anything they wish, as long as it pertains to holography.

My hope is that “we” here will focus on adding this to the other internet successes that have been a pillar in holography’s advancement in to the new millennium.

I’m sorry for being such a hard a** on certain individuals. I felt this needed to be talked about, as time is of the essence ...

I look forward to all comments

P.S. I was the student in the dark !
